name: Aurora Shader
what: Aurora curtains in one fragment shader: folded vertical rays from layered noise, a hem that bends toward the pointer, and an `hour` input (0–6) that moves the display from first glow through the 3 AM peak to dawn. Full-screen quad, one draw call.
use-when: Night, calm or time-of-night pages where the sky itself carries the story; text sits on its own dark panels.
avoid-when: Slop as a generic "aurora gradient" hero behind a SaaS headline; never as the only carrier of meaning.
reduced-motion: A CSS gradient poster tinted for the current hour; no shader.
touch: Touch points stir it too; never blocks scroll.
a11y: Decorative (aria-hidden). Paused off screen and in hidden tabs; DPR capped at 1.5.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/backgrounds)

name: Ben-Day Canvas
what: A real halftone on canvas: a drawn source is sampled on a rotated dot grid and every dot's radius follows the source's darkness. Dots near the pointer swell (Proximity Weight applied to dots), then settle back.
use-when: Pop-art, print and comic pages that need images in the page's own ink, responsive to presence.
avoid-when: Slop as a dotted overlay on photographs, or dots that animate on their own.
reduced-motion: Static halftone, no swell.
touch: The swell follows a finger while it is down; scroll is never blocked.
a11y: The canvas has the subject's alt text.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/backgrounds)

name: Case Number Ticker
what: A time-on-file counter (hh:mm:ss since this device first opened the case) that sits beside the case number.
use-when: The concept is an investigation, a log or a shift; one per site, in the frame, never in content.
avoid-when: Slop when used as a fake "live" stat, a countdown to nothing, or a number that pretends to be data.
reduced-motion: Same: it is a number that changes once a second; no animation is added.
touch: Same as desktop.
a11y: role="timer" with aria-live off, so screen readers are not interrupted every second.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/micro)

name: Chrome Blob
what: A liquid-chrome blob with real environment reflections (PMREM room environment), its surface breathing with noise. Drag to spin it; it coasts and springs back upright.
use-when: Y2K, product or playful pages that need one tactile 3D object as the hero, and nothing else in 3D.
avoid-when: Slop as a floating sphere behind a SaaS headline, or more than one per page.
reduced-motion: A static rendered poster of the blob (CSS radial chrome); no WebGL.
touch: Drag with a finger to spin; the page still scrolls vertically (touch-action pan-y).
a11y: Decorative (aria-hidden canvas); the label beside it carries the meaning.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/backgrounds)

name: Clay Suspect
what: A matte clay figure (SVG with a lit turbulence texture) you can press and drag to squash and stretch. Volume is preserved (width × height stays constant); on release it sags back slowly and keeps a thumbprint where you let go.
use-when: Claymation, toy-like or tactile pages where each figure stands for one real thing (here: one motion tier).
avoid-when: Slop as a mascot with nothing to say, or squash physics on buttons people need to trust.
reduced-motion: No squash; pressing still leaves the print.
touch: touch-action none on the figure only; a tap leaves a print.
a11y: Each figure is a button labelled with what it stands for; Enter or Space leaves a print and announces it.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/ui)

name: CT Scrubber
what: A vertical slice control for a layered volume: a range input styled as a scanner rail, with every layer's label stacked beside it like a deck index. The active slice's readout flips in on a split-flap board.
use-when: Any layered structure (strata, folders, floors, versions) where moving one cut through it explains what each layer holds.
avoid-when: Slop as a decorative slider with no layers behind it.
reduced-motion: The readout changes without flipping.
touch: The rail is a native range input, 48px wide hit area; labels are buttons.
a11y: Native range (aria-valuetext names the layer); index buttons jump to a layer; the readout is a polite live region.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/ui)

name: Custody Tag
what: A paper tag hanging on a string from a pin. Fling it and it swings as a damped pendulum; sign it and a new custody line is written on the back.
use-when: A single, important object needs a record of who touched it: an order, a document, a hand-off.
avoid-when: Slop as a decorative swinging thing with nothing written on it, or more than one per view.
reduced-motion: The tag hangs still; signing still adds the line instantly.
touch: Drag the tag sideways with a finger to swing it; the sign button is 48px.
a11y: The swing is decorative (aria-hidden); the custody list is a real ordered list and the button is labelled.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/micro)

name: Cut Ledger
what: An interactive Restraint Gate. Each candidate element carries its answers to the two gate questions; you keep or cut it and a live preview shows what is left.
use-when: Explaining an editorial decision, a design review, or any "why is this so empty" moment where the visitor can make the call themselves.
avoid-when: Slop as a decorative checklist with no consequence. The preview must change with every cut.
reduced-motion: Same controls; items leave the preview instantly instead of on the slow ease.
touch: Large toggle rows, 48px minimum.
a11y: Every row is a toggle button with aria-pressed; the preview count is announced politely.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/ui)

name: Dither Image
what: Renders any image (or a drawn source) through an ordered Bayer dither or Floyd–Steinberg error diffusion into a two- to four-colour palette, at a chosen pixel size.
use-when: Pixel-art, zine, retro-computing pages that need images in the page's own palette rather than photographs pasted in.
avoid-when: Slop as a filter on stock photos to fake a style, or on images whose detail the visitor needs.
reduced-motion: Same; it only re-renders when a control changes.
touch: Range inputs and buttons, 44px targets.
a11y: The canvas has the source's alt text; controls are labelled.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/backgrounds)

name: Freehand Pad
what: Draw on the page with a mouse, pen or finger. Stroke width follows speed and pen pressure (thin when fast, heavier when slow or pressed), strokes are smoothed with quadratic curves and saved to this device, with Undo and Clear.
use-when: Notebook, sketch or feedback pages where the visitor's own marks belong on the page.
avoid-when: Slop as a full-page doodle layer that steals scrolling, or anywhere drawings would be sent somewhere without saying so.
reduced-motion: Same; it has no animation of its own.
touch: touch-action none on the pad only; the rest of the page scrolls.
a11y: The pad is a labelled image region; Undo and Clear are buttons; drawing is optional to every task.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/cursor)

name: Gravity Flip
what: A small box of labelled objects under simple gravity, with floor and ceiling. One press reverses gravity and everything falls the other way, overshooting a little like it is underwater.
use-when: Surreal or playful pages where the physics of the page is itself the joke, and the labels carry real content.
avoid-when: Slop when the objects are unlabelled confetti or when it competes with a form or a reading task.
reduced-motion: Objects jump straight to their resting place on the new floor; no falling.
touch: The flip button is 48px; tap an object to nudge it.
a11y: Objects are list items with their labels; the button states the current direction with aria-pressed.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/ui)

name: Grid Overlay
what: Two switchable overlays drawn over a section: the column grid and the baseline grid, in the page's own units, so the visitor can check that everything sits where it says.
use-when: Swiss, editorial or systems pages where the grid is the argument and showing it is part of the content.
avoid-when: Slop as a permanent decorative grid behind a page that does not actually follow it.
reduced-motion: Same; the overlays switch instantly (they never animate).
touch: Two 48px toggle buttons.
a11y: Toggle buttons with aria-pressed; the overlays are aria-hidden.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/layout)

name: Heat Field
what: A low-resolution thermal field on a 2D canvas: heat diffuses and cools on a grid, the pointer is a warm source, and a colour ramp maps temperature to the palette. Scaled up and blurred by the browser, it reads as living colour under glass.
use-when: Under frosted glass or behind a single specimen, where the colour should feel alive and respond to presence.
avoid-when: Slop as a generic "animated gradient" behind text that must be read; text sits on glass, never on the field.
reduced-motion: One still frame of the field with three fixed warm spots; no simulation.
touch: Touch points are warm sources too; the canvas never blocks scroll.
a11y: Decorative, aria-hidden.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/backgrounds)

name: Hologram Volume
what: A point-cloud volume of stacked layers (one per data group, density from its count) with additive light, HUD rings and a clipping plane you move to cut the volume. Drag to orbit with damping; no auto-orbit.
use-when: Futuristic or data pages where a structure (folders, layers, strata) should be explored in space and sliced.
avoid-when: Slop as a spinning decorative globe or particle swarm with nothing to read; never without the poster path.
reduced-motion: The poster: still plates for each layer with their counts; no orbit.
touch: One-finger drag orbits inside the canvas only (touch-action pan-y keeps vertical page scroll).
a11y: The canvas is decorative; the caller renders the same layers as text (the slice readout).
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/backgrounds)

name: Hour Ledger
what: A ledger of time-stamped entries driven by an hour value (from scroll or a control): a large clock reads the exact time, the current row is lit by a slow lighthouse beam that sweeps on a fixed period, and past rows settle into ink.
use-when: Timelines told by the hour (a night, a launch, an incident) where one clock should move everything else.
avoid-when: Slop as a decorative clock with no entries, or with fabricated timestamps; every row must be real.
reduced-motion: The beam does not sweep; the current row is marked with a solid rule instead.
touch: Rows are buttons that set the hour.
a11y: The clock is a timer with aria-live off; the current row has aria-current="time"; rows are a list.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/scroll)

name: Identikit
what: A composite face built from flat SVG planes. Each feature (frame, brow, eyes, mouth) has a set of options; choosing one morphs the current shape into the next with MorphSVG, and the chosen name is reported back for a caption.
use-when: Vector, character or configurator pages where assembling something from parts is the content.
avoid-when: Slop as an avatar builder bolted onto a page about something else, or with realistic human faces.
reduced-motion: Features swap instantly, no morph.
touch: Options are buttons, 44px.
a11y: Each feature is a radio group; the face is role img with a live description of the current choices.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/ui)

name: Ink Writer
what: Text set in a handwriting face that writes itself line by line: a soft-edged mask sweeps along each line at a hand's pace (slower on long words), a nib dot rides the edge, and the ink settles darker as it dries.
use-when: Notebook, letter or journal pages where one short passage should appear as if being written now.
avoid-when: Slop for body copy, headings that must read on first paint, or more than one writing passage per screen.
reduced-motion: The passage is written already; no nib.
touch: Tap writes the rest at once.
a11y: The full text is real text from the start (the mask is visual only); aria-busy is never set.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/text)

name: Leader Countdown
what: An Academy film leader (number in a ring, crosshair, a sweeping wedge) driven by a 0–1 progress value you pass in, so scroll or a timeline counts it down from 5 to 2, then it cuts to black.
use-when: Opening each chapter of a film, tape or reel story; once per chapter, scrubbed.
avoid-when: Slop as a page loader or a decorative timer that is not tied to the story's timeline.
reduced-motion: Shows a still leader frame with the chapter number; no sweep.
touch: Nothing to touch.
a11y: Decorative (aria-hidden); the chapter title that follows is the real heading.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/scroll)

name: Measure Rule
what: A drawn dimension line under an element, with end ticks and its live width in pixels and in grid columns. It draws on when the element enters the viewport.
use-when: Grid-led pages where measurement is the voice: specimens, systems, Swiss layouts, technical documentation.
avoid-when: Slop under every heading, or with numbers that are not the element's real size.
reduced-motion: The rule is drawn already; the numbers are the same.
touch: Same as desktop.
a11y: The measurement is a visually small text line that screen readers also get, in words.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/type)

name: Melt Type Shader
what: A line of real type rendered to a texture and melted downward by a slow noise displacement in a fragment shader. The pointer warms the type and it runs faster near it.
use-when: One dreamlike statement on a surreal or uncanny page, where the type itself has to look unreliable.
avoid-when: Slop on body text, on anything the visitor must read quickly, or as a "cool shader" behind a normal page.
reduced-motion: The DOM text is shown solid, no shader is created.
touch: The melt runs on its own clock; touch warms it like the pointer.
a11y: The visible statement is real DOM text (visually hidden while the canvas is live), so it is read and selectable.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/backgrounds)

name: Rain Glass
what: Rain on a window at night, on a 2D canvas: falling streaks behind, and droplets on the glass that bead, merge and run down with a short trail. Neon from the palette is reflected in each drop.
use-when: Night, noir, cyberpunk or weather pages that need one atmospheric layer behind content that sits on its own solid panels.
avoid-when: Slop behind body text, or as a permanent loop on a page about something else.
reduced-motion: Rain stops: one still frame of drops on the glass.
touch: Same; it never captures input.
a11y: Decorative, aria-hidden. Pauses off screen and in hidden tabs.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/backgrounds)

name: Ransom Letters
what: A line of text set as cut-out letters, each in a different face, paper and angle from a list you pass in (seeded, so it is the same every visit). Every letter is a draggable piece with real z-order: the one you pick up comes to the top, tilts while held and lands slightly off.
use-when: Collage, zine or ransom-note pages where one short demand is the headline and mismatched type is the point.
avoid-when: Slop for anything longer than a few words, or with faces that are not otherwise used on the site.
reduced-motion: No tilt or landing settle; drag still works.
touch: Drag with a finger (touch-action none on each piece only).
a11y: The full line is the accessible name of the group (aria-label); individual letters are aria-hidden; arrow keys nudge a focused piece.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/type)

name: Redaction Reveal
what: Inline text under a black redaction bar. Hover, focus or tap lifts the bar for as long as you look; leaving puts it back. Reading is the interaction.
use-when: Editorial or investigative pages where a few key phrases should be earned by a closer look.
avoid-when: Slop on anything the visitor needs to act on (prices, legal text, instructions) or on more than a few phrases per screen.
reduced-motion: The bar lifts instantly; no slide.
touch: Tap toggles the bar (no hover on touch).
a11y: The words are real text inside a button with aria-pressed; screen readers always get the words; the bar is presentation only.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/text)

name: Reflow Photo
what: A captioned photograph you can drag through an article. On drop it is re-inserted between the nearest paragraphs and floats left or right of the column, and the text reflows around it.
use-when: Editorial and long-read layouts where the reader rearranging the page shows how the layout works.
avoid-when: Slop on short pages, or with images that are not part of the story.
reduced-motion: The photo jumps to its new slot without the settle; the reflow is the same.
touch: Long press is not needed: drag the photo with a finger (touch-action none on the photo only). Buttons move it up and down too.
a11y: "Move photo up" and "Move photo down" buttons do the same as dragging; the figure keeps its caption.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/layout)

name: Scissor Cut
what: Draw a closed path over a sheet of paper and it is cut out: the shape becomes a separate SVG piece (clip-path of the paper) that you can drag away, leaving a hole. Up to six cuts; the sheet can be replaced.
use-when: Collage and craft pages where cutting is the verb, or an onboarding moment that teaches drawing gestures.
avoid-when: Slop as a toy on a page with no paper metaphor; never on content the visitor needs to read whole.
reduced-motion: The cut piece appears beside the hole without the lift; dragging still works.
touch: Draw with a finger; touch-action none on the sheet only. A "Cut a square" button is the non-drawing path.
a11y: The sheet is a labelled region; the result is announced; the button does the same as a drawn cut.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/cursor)

name: Specimen Slide
what: Frosted glass slides you drag over a page. Each slide is a lens: outside it you read the label layer, through it you read the raw specimen layer aligned underneath. A specular edge follows the pointer.
use-when: Glass or lab pages where two readings of the same thing (label and raw data) should be compared in place.
avoid-when: Slop as decorative frosted cards over a gradient. Keep blur area small (it costs frames); never more than three slides.
reduced-motion: Slides lie in a still stack with the raw layer visible through them; dragging still works and settles instantly.
touch: Drag with a finger (touch-action none on slides only); arrow keys move a focused slide.
a11y: Both layers exist as text; each slide is a focusable labelled group; the raw layer is aria-hidden duplicates only.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/cursor)

name: Speech Bubble
what: A comic speech or thought bubble, pure CSS with an SVG tail, whose line types itself once the bubble enters the viewport, with a hard stop and a tiny impact shake.
use-when: Comic, pop or conversational layouts where a character (or the product) says one short real line.
avoid-when: Slop as decoration with no speaker, or for paragraphs; one or two sentences only.
reduced-motion: The full line is shown at once; no shake.
touch: Nothing to touch; tap replays the line.
a11y: The full line is in the DOM from the start (visually typed via a clip), so screen readers read it once and whole.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/text)

name: Spray Wall
what: A wall you spray-paint with the pointer on a 2D canvas: particle spray whose spread grows with distance from the wall (hold longer, it soaks), drips that run down under gravity when paint pools, an optional mask test (for stencils), and the finished wall saved on this device.
use-when: Graffiti, street or play pages where leaving a mark is the content.
avoid-when: Slop as a background effect on pages that are not about making marks; never over text the visitor must read.
reduced-motion: Spray still works; drips are drawn as short static runs instead of running.
touch: Spray with a finger (touch-action none on the wall only).
a11y: The wall is a labelled image region; colour choice, Clear and Save are buttons.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/cursor)

name: Spring Window
what: Desktop-style windows that pop open on a spring with overshoot, can be dragged by their title bar, brought to front, and closed. A small window manager in one component.
use-when: Y2K, OS-nostalgia or playful pages where facts are better found than listed, one per window.
avoid-when: Slop as fake error dialogs, pop-ups that block reading, or windows with nothing in them.
reduced-motion: Windows open and close instantly in a tidy cascade; dragging still works.
touch: Title bars are 44px tall drag handles; close buttons are 44px.
a11y: Each window is a labelled region; the close button is labelled; reopen buttons are listed for closed windows.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/ui)

name: Sprite Scene
what: A small playable canvas at 10 frames a second: a sprite walks a tiled map of rooms, picks up labelled items, and leaves a fading pixel wake. Keys, WASD or an on-screen pad.
use-when: Pixel-art or game-flavoured pages where exploring is the content: each item collected is a real fact.
avoid-when: Slop as an idle animation nobody can play, or a game that hides content the visitor needs.
reduced-motion: No idle animation and no wake; the sprite moves one tile per key press; every item is also listed as text.
touch: An on-screen pad with 48px buttons; the canvas does not capture scroll.
a11y: The canvas is a labelled image; the item list and pick-up announcements are real text (aria-live polite).
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/backgrounds)

name: Stakeout Terminal
what: A real, typeable terminal. Commands are answered from data you pass in (not canned text), each answer resolving from glyph noise left to right. History with the up arrow, tab completion, clear.
use-when: Developer tools, CLIs, cyberpunk or hacker-flavoured pages where trying commands is the fastest way to learn the product.
avoid-when: Slop as a fake terminal that types itself and cannot be used, or with commands that lie about the product.
reduced-motion: Answers appear instantly, no decode.
touch: The input is a normal text field; suggested commands are buttons.
a11y: The output is a log region (role="log", polite); the input is labelled; suggestions are buttons.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/ui)

name: Stencil Mask
what: A card stencil laid over a paintable surface: an SVG sheet with a shape cut out of it, plus a hit test (Path2D in the surface's coordinates) the paint tool uses to keep spray inside the cut. Lifting the stencil leaves the sharp-edged mark.
use-when: Spray, print or craft surfaces where masking is part of the making; pair with a paint surface that accepts a mask test.
avoid-when: Slop as a static decorative cut-out with nothing to paint.
reduced-motion: The stencil appears and lifts without the slide.
touch: Stencil choices and Lift are buttons.
a11y: Stencil options are a radio group; the sheet is decorative.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/cursor)

name: Stroke Draw
what: Any set of SVG paths draws itself on (stroke-dashoffset from each path's real length) when it enters the viewport or when its key changes, path by path, with an optional nib dot riding the line.
use-when: Vector, technical or sketch pages where seeing a line being drawn explains construction.
avoid-when: Slop on icons in a feature grid, or redrawing every time something scrolls past.
reduced-motion: Paths are drawn already.
touch: Nothing to touch.
a11y: The svg takes a title from the caller (role img + aria-label); paths are presentation.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/scroll)

name: Subtraction Room
what: A crowded room of labels that scroll empties one at a time, on one slow ease, logging every cut in the margin until one word is left.
use-when: A minimal page has to prove its restraint: the visitor watches what was removed, so the empty result reads as a decision.
avoid-when: Slop when the "removed" items are filler invented to be cut, or when the final word is a tagline. Cut real candidates.
reduced-motion: The room is shown already empty, the full cut ledger printed beside the last word. Nothing animates.
touch: Same scroll; the ledger moves under the word on narrow screens.
a11y: The cut ledger is a real ordered list; removed labels are aria-hidden once cut; the final word is a heading.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/scroll)

name: Tag Drag Wall
what: A wall of mixed objects on up to seven parallax depths. Every object wears a museum tag; drag one and it lags into a small rotation, its tag swings and its custody line updates.
use-when: Maximal, collected, archive-like pages where the clutter is the content and the visitor should be allowed to rearrange it.
avoid-when: Slop when the objects are random decoration with no tags, or when the wall hides the one thing the page must say.
reduced-motion: No parallax and no swing; dragging still moves objects, which land exactly where dropped.
touch: Pointer events with capture; touch-action none on objects only, so the page still scrolls between them.
a11y: Each object is a focusable figure; arrow keys nudge it 16px; its tag text is its caption. Custody updates are announced politely.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/layout)

name: Tape Deck
what: Transport controls (rewind, play, pause, fast-forward) with two SVG reels and a timecode counter that drive the page's scroll inside one section. The reels spin at the real scroll speed, so scrolling by hand turns them too.
use-when: A scrubbed scroll story (a reel, a tape, a timeline) where giving the visitor transport buttons makes the scroll position feel like media.
avoid-when: Slop on a normal page with no timeline, or autoplaying on load.
reduced-motion: Buttons jump between chapter marks instead of rolling; reels do not spin.
touch: 48px buttons; the deck never captures scroll.
a11y: A labelled toolbar; buttons have aria-pressed for the active mode; the counter is a timer with aria-live off.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/scroll)

name: Tarot Deck
what: A fanned deck of cards. The deck leans gently toward the pointer (Considerate Magnet) and steps back when it leaves; drawing a card lifts it out of the fan and flips it in 3D to a face with one real fact. Draws are random without repeats until the deck is spent.
use-when: Playful, editorial or bohemian pages where facts are better discovered one at a time than listed.
avoid-when: Slop for content the visitor needs all at once, or as fortune-telling with made-up claims; every face must be true.
reduced-motion: Cards turn without the lift and flip; the lean is off.
touch: Tap "Draw a card"; no lean on touch.
a11y: A button draws; the drawn face is a live region; every fact is also listed in a details element.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/ui)

name: Thumbprint
what: A procedural fingerprint (whorl of offset ellipse arcs, seeded) pressed into a surface as an inset SVG. Same seed, same print.
use-when: Tactile, clay, forensic or handmade pages where the visitor's touch should leave a mark that stays.
avoid-when: Slop as a decorative "security" icon, or anywhere it suggests real biometrics.
reduced-motion: Same; the print appears without the press-in scale.
touch: Works the same for finger and pointer.
a11y: Decorative (aria-hidden); the action that made it is announced by its caller.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/micro)

name: Velvet Curtain
what: Two heavy velvet panels (folds from layered gradients, a gold fringe) that part on entry with a weighted ease and a slight gather at the top, and draw closed again when the section leaves the viewport, ready to part on return.
use-when: A single theatrical reveal on archival, period or stage pages; the content behind must stand on its own once open.
avoid-when: Slop as a page loader, on every section, or hiding content that must be read on arrival (it opens within a second).
reduced-motion: The curtains are drawn open and tied back at the sides; no motion.
touch: Same; it never blocks taps once open (pointer-events none).
a11y: Decorative (aria-hidden); content behind is in the DOM and reachable at all times.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/scroll)

name: Wax Seal
what: Press a wax seal onto anything: a blob of wax with an irregular seeded edge, an embossed monogram (inner shadow and highlight, no images), a press-in animation with a short spread, and the sealed state kept on this device.
use-when: Certifying, approving or "filing" one item at a time on archival, formal or letter-like pages.
avoid-when: Slop as decoration on every card, or as a fake trust badge; a seal must record something the visitor did.
reduced-motion: The seal appears pressed, no squash or spread.
touch: It is a button; tap seals and tap again breaks the seal.
a11y: A toggle button (aria-pressed) with a label naming what is sealed.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/micro)

name: Wind Botanical
what: Pressed-herbarium SVG plants (stems with leaves along a spine) that sway in a wind field: a faint constant breeze plus gusts made by the pointer's horizontal speed. Each stem bends from its base with spring damping; leaves flutter with a phase offset.
use-when: Botanical, bohemian or natural pages that need one living layer framing the content, not behind text.
avoid-when: Slop as decoration under paragraphs, or perpetual motion with nothing causing it (the breeze must stay faint).
reduced-motion: Plants are drawn still, no sway.
touch: Touch drags make wind too; scroll is never blocked.
a11y: Decorative, aria-hidden. Pauses off screen.
status: candidate to contribute back to the skill (examples/components/backgrounds)
